prompt: What is the one task a model is trained on during pretraining?
hint: Grammar and facts were not taught as subjects.

choices.text: Answering questions people have rated as helpful
choices.why: That is the tuning that comes after, on conversations.

choices.text: Predicting the next token of a text
choices.why: Right. Everything else it learnt was learnt because it helped with this.

choices.text: Looking up facts in a database of public pages
choices.why: There is no database inside; what it learnt is in the weights.

choices.text: Translating between the languages of its corpus
choices.why: It may learn to translate, as a side effect of predicting text.

prompt: Which of these does an open model hand you along with its weights? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A tokenizer
choices.why: Yes: without it the weights cannot read text.

choices.text: A chat template
choices.why: Yes: it lives beside the weights, in the tokenizer's configuration.

choices.text: A licence
choices.why: Yes: it says what you may do with the rest.

choices.text: The text it was trained on
choices.why: The card describes the training data; the data itself does not ship.

choices.text: An API key for its makers' service
choices.why: An open model runs on your machine; there is nothing to call.

prompt: Llama 3.1 was trained on about 15 trillion tokens of public text. What does that tell ana about Lantern Books' orders?
hint: Where would the order history have come from?

choices.text: That a model of that size has probably seen them
choices.why: Size is not access. The orders were never public.

choices.text: That it knows the ones placed before December 2023
choices.why: The cutoff limits public text; private records were never in it at any date.

choices.text: Nothing: they were never in its training text
choices.why: Right. What a model knows is what was in its text, and the shop's records were not.

choices.text: That it can find them if the prompt asks politely
choices.why: No prompt retrieves what was never learnt; the fact has to be put in the prompt.

prompt: A base model is given a question. Why might it answer with three more questions?

choices.text: It continues text, and in the text it learnt from, questions come in runs
choices.why: Right. It is doing its job; its job is not answering you.

choices.text: Its weights were damaged in the download, so it answers at random and must be fetched again
choices.why: A base model behaving like this is working as designed.

choices.text: Its temperature is set too high
choices.why: Temperature changes how it picks words, not whether it treats the text as a turn to answer.

choices.text: It refuses questions it cannot verify
choices.why: A base model has no notion of refusing; that is learnt in tuning.

prompt: Meta's document says one token is generated only by base models. What does an instruction-tuned Llama emit instead when its reply is done?
hint: Its name means the end of a turn.

choices.text: `<|end_of_text|>`, like the base model
choices.why: That is the one the document reserves for base models.

choices.text: `<|begin_of_text|>`, to start the next turn
choices.why: That opens the whole prompt, once.

choices.text: `<|eot_id|>`, end of turn
choices.why: Right. The server stops generating when it sees it.

choices.text: Nothing: it stops when it reaches its token limit
choices.why: The limit is a ceiling; a tuned model ends well before it.

prompt: ana downloads a model from a hub, runs it locally on a support e-mail, and it replies by writing another customer e-mail. What is the likeliest explanation?
hint: Look at the name she downloaded.

choices.text: The model does not support Portuguese
choices.why: A language problem produces a poor answer, not a continuation in the same form.

choices.text: She took the base model rather than the instruct one
choices.why: Right. It loads, runs, and continues the text instead of answering it.

choices.text: The e-mail is longer than the model's window allows
choices.why: An over-long prompt is refused or truncated; it does not change the model's kind.

choices.text: Running models locally always degrades their answers
choices.why: The same weights give the same behaviour wherever they run.

prompt: What does the chat template turn a list of messages into?

choices.text: A JSON object that the network parses role by role, keeping each message apart
choices.why: JSON is how an API receives it; the network never sees JSON.

choices.text: One string, with the roles written in as special tokens
choices.why: Right. Section 08 printed one.

choices.text: A summary of the earlier turns, kept short to save tokens
choices.why: Nothing is summarised; every turn is written out.

choices.text: Separate calls to the model, one per message
choices.why: The whole conversation is read in one pass.

prompt: Why does the rendered string end with an assistant header and nothing after it?
hint: What does the model do with any text it is given?

choices.text: To leave room for the system prompt to be added later
choices.why: The system prompt is already at the start of the string.

choices.text: Because the template file was cut short
choices.why: It ends there on purpose, as Meta's document shows.

choices.text: So that continuing the text means writing the assistant's turn
choices.why: Right. Continuing text is its only skill, and the template points it at the reply.

choices.text: To mark the conversation as finished
choices.why: The conversation is waiting for exactly one more turn.

prompt: A prompt that works well on one model family does worse on another, with the same messages. Which explanation does section 08 support?
hint: What sits between the messages and the network?

choices.text: Each reads the turns through its own template and tuning
choices.why: Right. Same messages, different sequence and different learnt conventions.

choices.text: The second API drops the system prompt
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson suggests an API drops it; it is written into the sequence.

choices.text: Prompts only work on the model they were first written for
choices.why: They transfer often enough; the point is that transfer has to be measured.

choices.text: The second family has a smaller vocabulary of special tokens
choices.why: The size of the vocabulary is not what changes the behaviour.

prompt: What does 'supported' mean in a model card's list of languages?

choices.text: Every language that appeared in the training text
choices.why: The same card says it was trained on more than the supported ones.

choices.text: The tokenizer can encode its alphabet
choices.why: Encoding text is not the same as being tested on it.

choices.text: The makers tested it and stand behind the results
choices.why: Right. A language outside the list is one nobody measured.

choices.text: The licence permits use in that country
choices.why: Languages and licence terms are separate parts of the card.

prompt: Why does section 09 say to read a card's evaluations for their shape rather than their scores?

choices.text: Because the scores are invented by marketing
choices.why: The lesson does not say that, and it is not why.

choices.text: Because a higher benchmark score comes with a slower and more expensive model in production
choices.why: Speed is a separate criterion, measured separately.

choices.text: Because shapes are easier to remember than numbers
choices.why: Memorability is not the argument.

choices.text: Because they measured someone else's task, in their languages, with their examples
choices.why: Right. Which tasks and languages were measured tells you whether any of it applies.

prompt: What a closed provider publishes that ana must read, in place of a full card, is the list of model identifiers and their ___ dates.
hint: Lesson 2 reads them from the sheet.

prompt: What is a model's knowledge cutoff?

choices.text: The last date its makers will answer questions about it
choices.why: Support dates are something else.

choices.text: When the text it was trained on stops
choices.why: Right. Nothing after that date is in what it learnt.

choices.text: The date it will be retired from the API
choices.why: That is a retirement date, which lesson 2 reads.

choices.text: The longest prompt it accepts
choices.why: That is the context window.

prompt: Match each thing the model lacks to what supplies it.

pairs.right: Retrieval from a trusted source, or a newer model
Retrieval from the shop's own systems

pairs.left: Stock of one title right now
pairs.right: A tool the model can call

prompt: For sorting Lantern Books' e-mail into five labels, how much should a later knowledge cutoff weigh in ana's choice?
hint: What facts does the task need?

choices.text: Very little: the task needs no public fact newer than the language
choices.why: Right. A later date helps tasks about the world, and this one is about an e-mail.

choices.text: A lot: customers mention recent books
choices.why: The label depends on what the customer wants, not on knowing the book.

choices.text: It decides everything, since an older model cannot read new e-mails
choices.why: Reading an e-mail needs the language, which has not changed.

choices.text: As much as the price, because both change every month
choices.why: The cutoff is fixed per model; it is not a monthly variable.

prompt: Put the four ways of adapting a model in order, from the cheapest to build and keep to the dearest.
trap: Retrieval is a system to keep running, but it still costs less to keep than a tuned model.

prompt: A model answers in the right format but does not know the shop's refund rules. Which step fixes that gap?

choices.text: More examples of the output format
choices.why: The format is already right; examples teach format.

choices.text: Fine-tuning on last year's tickets
choices.why: That can teach a style, and freezes the rules as they were.

choices.text: Retrieving the rules into the prompt
choices.why: Right. Missing facts are retrieval's gap, and it keeps up when the rules change.

choices.text: A shorter prompt
choices.why: Removing text cannot supply a missing fact.

prompt: Someone proposes fine-tuning a model on this month's stock levels so it can answer stock questions. What is wrong with the plan?

choices.text: Fine-tuning cannot be done on numbers
choices.why: Numbers are text like anything else.

choices.text: It would be out of date before the training run ended
choices.why: Right. Facts that move belong in the prompt at request time.

choices.text: A base model is needed, and providers do not sell them
choices.why: Open collections publish base models; that is not the flaw.

choices.text: Nothing; it is the standard way to add facts
choices.why: It is the expensive way to discover that retrieval was the answer.

prompt: Through an API, which of a model's five parts do you hold yourself?

choices.text: The tokenizer and the template, the provider keeps the weights
choices.why: The provider tokenizes and applies its template too.

choices.text: All five, downloaded on first use
choices.why: Nothing is downloaded; you call an address.

choices.text: None; you send messages to an endpoint
choices.why: Right. The provider runs all five behind one address.

choices.text: Only the licence, which you accept by signing up
choices.why: Signing up accepts terms of service, which are not the model's licence.

prompt: Match each Llama 3.1 special token to what it does.
hint: Meta's prompt_format.md, quoted in sections 07 and 08.

pairs.right: Opens the name of a role
Ends generation in a base model

prompt: ana's sorting prompt fails on borderline e-mails: the model knows the task but puts some refunds under order-status. Following section 11, what does she try first?
hint: The model understands; the borderline is the gap.

choices.text: Retrieving the shop's whole refund policy into every request she sends
choices.why: The model is not missing a fact; it is drawing a line in the wrong place.

choices.text: A few hard cases, each with its answer
choices.why: Right. Examples are the step for a task understood and a boundary missed.

choices.text: Fine-tuning on every e-mail the shop has received
choices.why: That skips two cheaper steps that fix exactly this.

choices.text: Switching to a model with a later cutoff
choices.why: Nothing in a borderline e-mail depends on recent facts.
